$$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(\frac{2}{3}{x}^{4})) \\  & =3\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡(\frac{2}{3}{x}^{4})) \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{{(\frac{2}{3}{x}^{4})}^{2}+1}}\cdot {(\frac{2}{3}{x}^{4})}^{′} \\  & =3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac{4}{9}{x}^{8}+1}}\cdot \frac{8}{3}{x}^{3} \\  & =8\cdot \frac{{x}^{3}}{\sqrt{\frac{4{x}^{8}+9}{9}}} \\  & =\frac{24{x}^{3}}{\sqrt{4{x}^{8}+9}}.\end{aligned}
$$
